patch_description: The current pipeline's final stage re-weights already-smoothed data with a Python loop, adding both compute cost and residual group delay (the exponential weights emphasize the window start-relative position, shifting the effective evaluation point backward and inflating lag_error to 0.41). This edit (1) replaces the per-sample loop with a single `np.convolve` using a precomputed weight vector (identical math, O(n) instead of O(n·W) Python overhead), and (2) spends the recovered efficiency on a light inter-window slope-consistency pass: we estimate noise σ robustly via MAD of the input's first differences, and wherever consecutive filtered values differ by less than 0.5σ — i.e., the difference is statistically indistinguishable from noise and cannot represent a genuine trend change — we snap the sample toward a 5-tap running median blend. This directly attacks slope_changes (41.2) and false_reversals (36.6) without touching genuine dynamics, since real trend changes exceed the noise floor. The smoothing kernel is also rebalanced toward the window's later samples to shave a bit of phase lag, improving responsiveness_score and correlation.
